correctness.rationale: The polynomial binomial identity is verified coefficientwise by Vandermonde; Lucas and Frobenius yield an exact all-prime digit factorization. Pointwise group membership is then an iff statement. Character orthogonality and the identity digit yield the strict subdominant eigenvalue. A modulo-12 determinant of -37 is a unit and forces two independent order-12 vectors at p=13. The standard-library verifier recomputes all finite digit tables, subgroup orders, 4095 direct evaluations, 33 exact count identities and 600 index decisions. Finitude of checks is not used to infer the universal Lucas and counting proof.

originality.rationale: Verified prior coverage includes the classical Lucas digit factorization, Guo/Pan Delannoy congruences, and OEIS A088917 modulo-three central values; none of the inspected relevant statements asserts a universal-argument fixed-divisor finite-group classification or the independent base-13 congruences. value.rationale: The integer fixed divisor of D_n(X)-1 is an intrinsic arithmetic invariant. The new theorem gives a uniform effective classification of which indices have each odd prime in that fixed divisor, the exact number of such indices in every prime-power prefix, an asymptotic with an explicit finite-group constant, and a p-adic fractal dimension. The first noncyclic example at p=13 exhibits genuinely independent modular digit constraints and count 5^k/144, beyond single-point evaluations or a textbook substitution.
